sapience_notes.subject: stall re-prompt recovery for the stack-PR-submission task's Phase 3
sapience_notes.value: Two consecutive dispatch_seq-28 attempts at the same phase died mid-flight without writing .return-meta.json/.orchestrator-handoff.json, but their code (review-stack-prepare.sh's cut/show/record-request machinery plus a 38-case test suite) had already been committed cleanly. The recovery dispatch needed zero new implementation -- only foreground re-verification and the plan/progress/handoff/commit closure sequence the prior attempts never reached. This confirms that a stalled-dispatch re-prompt should start by reading committed git state before assuming any work is missing.

sapience_notes.subject: verify-touched.sh scoped battery finding classification for review-stack-prepare.sh
sapience_notes.value: Phase 3's scoped verify-touched.sh run surfaced two findings that both turned out non-blocking: (1) test-verify-deploy-context-budget.sh correctly reports source/deployed-tree content drift for review-stack-prepare.sh, its test, and orchestrator-runtime-files.md, plus an index-entries.json line_count mismatch (729 vs 730 for the orchestrator-runtime-files.md entry) -- this is EXPECTED because the plan's own Phase 3 'Files to modify' note and Phase 7's task list both state the index-entries.json line_count is reconciled by Phase 7's deploy-headless.sh redeploy, not before; (2) test-orchestrate-recover-outcome.sh case 3 failed once under the full 74-suite parallel run but passed 7/7 in three standalone re-runs, indicating an mtime-window timing flake under heavy concurrent batch load rather than a real regression.

sapience_notes.subject: review-stack-prepare.sh cut subcommand's commit-tree construction never touches the shared working tree
sapience_notes.value: rsp_cut_execute builds each unit's review commit entirely via a private GIT_INDEX_FILE overlay (rsp_overlay_tree) and git commit-tree/git update-ref compare-and-swap, with the moved-base case additionally using git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base for a non-interactive three-way move -- never git checkout, git merge, or git rebase. Verified empirically: a suite case asserts byte-identical HEAD, .git/index, and git status before and after a cut.
